I've saved the Q3 2025 answers to `/work/answer.json`. Run the same way on Q2, my code reproduces all 10 of your reference values.

| Question | Q3 answer |
|---|---|
| a. Segment with the highest net sales | smb, 351,298,206 |
| b. Customers with a paid order | 248 |
| c. Category with the highest net sales | acc, 327,949,326 |
| d. Month with the highest net sales | 2025-08 |
| e. Customer with the largest total refunds | u190@ex.com |
| f. Customers with 2 or more paid orders | 237 |
| g. Average net sales per order | 751,603 |
| h. September vs. August growth | -2.6% |

To match your Q2 numbers, I had to make three interpretations beyond your definitions:
- **Dates are in Korean time.** Order times are stored in UTC, and the quarter and month boundaries only match your numbers after converting to Korean time (UTC+9). With plain UTC, Q2's h comes out as 8.6 instead of 0.6.
- **Segment labels are cleaned up.** The data has variants like " consumer" and "Enterprise "; I trimmed spaces and lowercased them so each segment counts once. That's why a is written in lowercase as "smb".
- **A customer is one email address.** There are 300 customer records but only 250 distinct emails, so I counted customers by email for b, e and f. Counting by record ID gives 277 and 218 for Q2's b and f, which doesn't match your 234 and 194.

The calculation script is at `/tmp/s/a.py`.
